To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

student teachers' views on what they needed to learn for teaching science changed during their course of study, and that they were aware of the importance of their personal development in becoming a teacher.

the students' views of the nature of science knowledge for teaching changed over time, that the students' own learning was an important source for their development and that they had developed a personal approach to learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of student teachers as learners of science and of their views of the knowledge they have acquired.
the nature and development of knowledge for teaching, the processes by which students develop, and their perceptions of their own progress and the influences on their learning.

the development of student teachers' understanding of scientific ideas and the knowledge they need to teach the primary curriculum, the sources they draw upon for their learning, and how they see their own learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the students' knowledge, attitudes, beliefs and confidence in their science teaching had increased.
the student teachers1 knowledge of the nature of science, their understanding of scientific phenomena, and their ability to teach science, had been enhanced.

the students1 learning and development was complex, and that it was important to collect multiple sources of information in order to gain an insight into the nature of the learning and the processes of change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the students1 learning of science and their personal development as teachers was complex.
it was necessary to collect individual students' accounts of their experiences of learning and to record their views.
the personal dimension is important but not privileged over the other aspects of teacher learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should not be afraid to ask students to talk to us about their experiences and their feelings (p.68).
we need to be more sensitive to the complexity of individual development and to the importance of understanding the personal and social dimensions of change. (p.68).
